## PCR-BUSTER-ENGINE-001

**Capability work is missing from the attempt budget**

Status: in-progress. Severity: high.

### Problem and impact

The attempt resource receipt measures the provider process. It does not exclusively own and account for all capability, browser, adapter, and completion work that Buster launches.

A cheap provider can report low resource usage while its other local work exceeds the claimed CPU, memory or process budget.

### Components and current state

- Buster Runner
- Provider process
- Capability RPC
- Report adapters
- Shared Worker Core

Core now performs early and final resource observations. runner.measure still reads instance.resources(); moving the observation later does not create exclusive whole-attempt ownership. Related locally closed Prism/Core findings are not reopened. Durable fixture readiness/control, separate readiness/completion promises, a bounded fourth process pipe and native launcher ownership primitives exist as locally tested building blocks. The production runner still constructs LocalWorkerRuntime; the native lifetime API is not its production execution path.

### Remaining work

- Integrate durable attempt/claim-bound local execution ownership across Core and Buster, including provider work, parent capability execution, browser/command children, adapters, evidence and finalization.
- Define aggregate measurement and hard budget enforcement. Distinguish cumulative CPU from CPU rate and processes from cgroup tasks. Required missing observations must fail. Declare remote BuildKit/Kubernetes work separately.
- Preserve retained fixtures through durable ownership transfer, fences and crash recovery; coordinate with PCR-BUSTER-ENGINE-004.
- Connect the actual Buster attempt host, restricted role-specific launch policy/broker and durable fixture lifetime to the runner. Keep broker and capability work inside the attempt scope. After the verified cutover remove the superseded executable runner, file-capability launch and sampling paths; retain no executable fallback.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- Run the original provider in an actual delegated cgroup. Keep its own load small and launch two real capability children whose combined load exceeds the attempt budget although individual limits pass.
- Put load separately in the report adapter and finalization. Compare the original receipt and terminal state with aggregate counters; unrelated concurrent service work must not be charged to this attempt.
- Exercise short-lived children, descendants surviving their leader, missing counters, cancellation and drain failure. Fake cgroup files are not positive containment evidence.

### Completion criteria

- Every claimed local phase has exclusive ownership or demonstrably non-overlapping equivalent accounting.
- Aggregate overrun or missing required observations prevent completed; successful drain leaves no local work running.
- Original Core/Buster claim, timeout, fixture and evidence guarantees remain covered.
- Fixture readiness is journaled before dependency acknowledgement, teardown fences acknowledgement races, and only the original Core terminal journal seals completion. Historical readiness cannot authorize new dependents.

### Separate environment acceptance

Actual delegated cgroups and real providers/browsers are required. Acceptance in the deployed worker container is separate.

### Dependencies

- [PCR-BUSTER-ENGINE-004](#pcr-buster-engine-004)

## PCR-BUSTER-ENGINE-004

**Restarted terminal jobs retain source workspaces without a durable quiescence proof**

Status: partially-implemented. Severity: medium.

### Problem and impact

After a worker or host crash there is no durable proof that every process belonging to a job has stopped. Source and working directories therefore remain retained.

Repeated interrupted jobs can consume disk and quotas. Deleting from terminal metadata alone could remove inputs still used by live descendants.

### Components and current state

- Buster RemotePlanService
- terminal-workspace
- Provider/capability/adapter ownership

Normal confirmed execution cleans inputs. Durable status write and read failures stop admission; shutdown waits for pending admission writes. recover() explicitly retains inputs because a terminal record does not prove orphan quiescence.

### Remaining work

- Publish durable job/attempt/claim ownership before launch and include capability children, adapters and retained fixtures.
- On restart reconcile the exact fenced owner and require authoritative complete termination. Preserve and diagnose unknown ownership instead of guessing.
- Authorize the existing narrow idempotent input cleanup only after that proof; preserve valid result, evidence and log receipts.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- Crash and restart the original worker with a live provider plus actual capability/adapter children. Distinguish leader death from complete process termination.
- Exercise crash windows around ownership publication, drain and file removal; reused or namespace-mismatched PIDs must never authorize cleanup.
- Read completed/failed/cancelled job receipts and retained-fixture transitions after restart.

### Completion criteria

- No active or uncertain owner loses its inputs.
- After complete quiescence is proved, only authorized inputs are removed; repeated recovery is safe.
- Real quota release and retained result/evidence access are demonstrated on original jobs.

### Separate environment acceptance

Native crash and containment tests are required. Log retention and external demo lifetime are independent of source-workspace cleanup.

### Dependencies

- [PCR-BUSTER-ENGINE-001](#pcr-buster-engine-001)

### Evidence boundary

Source inspection only; no test rerun and no live acceptance performed.

## PCR-OBS-002

**Confirmed run history lacks complete connected retirement**

Status: partially-implemented. Severity: medium.

### Problem and impact

Confirmed history still lacks a complete release protocol understood by every reader and component that can reopen, accept or replay it.

Partial compaction can leave record, metadata, evidence and blob quotas exhausted. Uncoordinated deletion could lose evidence or protection against repeated external actions.

### Components and current state

- RecordStore
- Attempt/Admission
- ArtifactStore
- Buster jobs
- Nova dispatch/import
- Operator delivery

Telemetry, admission, imported attempt results, redundant dispatch archive copies and causal operator projections have bounded implementations and local evidence. They do not remove all job counts, evidence objects or shared blobs. The dispatch projection has a real one-POST replay result while retaining logical job, receipt and source blob. Its native provider execution failed; that failure does not invalidate the bounded storage transition or prove successful native execution.

### Remaining work

- Inventory active/completed owners, all current reopen/accept/read/replay consumers and shared references.
- Implement explicit manual release with durable consumer completion and required idempotency/uncertainty tombstones, atomically across those consumers. Keep every still-required reference resolvable.
- Release actual byte and record quotas rather than moving data into unaccounted sidecars. D07 does not permit automatic age-based log deletion.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- Use small real store quotas with active, waiting and completed runs and shared artifacts; measure actual bytes and entries before/after authorized release.
- Replay old deliveries after restart and exercise competing writers and SIGKILL between durable transitions.
- Use original result, evidence, artifact and operator readers on retired and deliberately retained history.

### Completion criteria

- Only authorized and fully confirmed history is released; active and uncertain work remains intact.
- Released capacity admits new actual writes. Replays do not repeat an external action or fabricate delivery outcomes.
- All affected consumers understand the same retirement state and retain the existing projection guarantees.

### Separate environment acceptance

Original local store/process tests can close this implementation scope. Cleanup of real user data remains a separate operational action.

### Dependencies

No dependency on another entry in this register is established.

### Evidence boundary

Source inspection only; no test rerun and no live acceptance performed.

- **recorded verification:** Partial: telemetry, admission and imported attempt-result copies were checked with actual quota release and preserved replay. Independent attempt-v2 checks: 19/19. Integrated root checks: 45/45, no skips. Complete retention across the remaining stores and references remains open.
- **implementation commit:** 27315faad862f71df940ed32bc4e5a98eca72e0d

## IFR-21-001

**Runtime image rebuild inputs are not fully reproducible**

Status: in-progress. Severity: medium.

### Problem and impact

A source commit still does not bind all browser archives and time-dependent scanner databases; complete image rebuilds have not been compared.

The same source can produce different installed content or scan results. Source pinning does not guarantee byte-identical images.

### Components and current state

- versions.json
- Runtime Dockerfiles
- Playwright downloads
- Trivy databases

Python transitive locks, Go modules, binary checksums and apt snapshots have partial fixes backed by real installations/builds. ARM64 wheel resolution is not ARM64 execution. Complete image builds and browser launches remain outstanding.

### Remaining work

- Bind browser archives to independently verified hashes. Preserve Trivy refresh data as explicit reproducible inputs while recording scan freshness separately.
- Define architecture and builder/provenance inputs, then compare two complete isolated builds from identical selections.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- RUNTIME_LOCK_PYTHON="$PYTHON_311" node --test tests/verification/deployment/runtime-tool-locks-native.mjs
- RUNTIME_LOCK_GO="$SELECTED_GO" node --test tests/verification/deployment/go-tool-locks-native.mjs
- Build complete images twice with independent empty caches and identical source, architecture, browser/database bytes and builder settings. Compare package inventory, SBOM and output digests.

### Completion criteria

- All remaining time-dependent inputs are explicitly bound.
- Two actual complete builds exist; every package/SBOM/digest difference is explained against the selected rebuild contract.
- Actual selected browsers and tools execute. Claim ARM64 runtime support only after actual ARM64 execution.

### Separate environment acceptance

Complete isolated image/browser tests are required. Deployment of verified output digests and ARM64 live acceptance remain separate.

### Dependencies

No dependency on another entry in this register is established.

## IFR-10-001

**Long-lived rootless BuildKit lacks a job-specific process boundary**

Status: open. Severity: high.

### Problem and impact

The long-lived rootless BuildKit uses --net=host and --oci-worker-no-process-sandbox; the missing process sandbox is an unresolved security boundary for untrusted Dockerfile RUN work.

Project code may affect the shared build process environment or leave processes running. Supervisor secret access or privilege escalation has not been demonstrated.

### Components and current state

- Buster runtime
- rootlesskit/BuildKit
- Build provider
- Shared cache

Both flags remain in docker/buster-runtime-entrypoint.sh. Rootless UID/file permissions and a separate supervisor identity do not by themselves provide the missing job process boundary.

### Remaining work

- Run untrusted builds in an ephemeral dedicated security/process boundary, outside long-lived control and credential processes.
- Define connected cache/file/network access and cleanup guarantees for the exact pinned runtime image.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- Using the real runtime image, execute two distinct build jobs and negatively test unauthorized process visibility, signals and background processes surviving job completion.
- Test cross-job file/cache access and unauthorized network egress. A successful rootless startup probe is insufficient.

### Completion criteria

- Build jobs cannot influence unrelated control/job processes or continue after confirmed completion.
- Allowed cache/network paths and forbidden cross-job access are demonstrated with real builds.

### Separate environment acceptance

Isolated native security tests on the pinned image are required; accept the actual host/container boundary separately.

### Dependencies

No dependency on another entry in this register is established.

### Evidence boundary

## IFR-01-001

**Automated host bootstrap and restore prerequisites are incomplete**

Status: open. Severity: medium.

### Problem and impact

The repository setup assumes an existing cluster; the effective host/K3s/storage starting environment is not a fully reproducible bootstrap and restore contract.

After host loss or on a new host, versions, datastore, disk and application dependencies must be reconstructed. The setup name alone can overstate its coverage.

### Components and current state

- K3s/host
- Host bootstrap automation
- scripts/deploy.sh
- Storage provisioner
- Paperless dependencies

Installation and setup documents start from an existing cluster. The repository has no supported empty-host automation. It cannot install and configure K3s, establish storage and independent access, or emit a reproducible host record. The repository records no effective cluster configuration, and generic K3s defaults do not replace actual operator settings.

### Remaining work

- Record redacted actual host/K3s versions, startup flags, datastore, API requirements, CNI, StorageClass/CSI and cgroup preparation.
- Implement one reviewed, idempotent host-bootstrap entry point with prerequisite checks, a dry-run or plan view, explicit stop conditions and bounded rollback before irreversible changes.
- Automate the selected K3s, datastore, DNS, CNI, storage and independent-administration preparation without storing credentials in Git or combining an unproved CNI migration with application deployment.
- Emit a redacted machine-readable record of effective versions, flags, network ranges, storage ownership and recovery inputs.
- Hand off to scripts/deploy.sh only after the platform checks pass.
- Document host backup, key/credential ownership, Paperless dependencies and independent administration with a restore sequence.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- On an isolated empty host, use only the completed documented procedure.
- After restore verify API, DNS, storage, pipeline and required Paperless data; treat every undocumented prerequisite supplied manually as a gap.

### Completion criteria

- Another operator can use the reviewed automation and documented external inputs to build the selected cluster from an empty supported host without undocumented manual preparation.
- A repeated run is safe, the plan and effective host record are reviewable, and every irreversible action has a stated stop and recovery boundary.
- The automated handoff deploys no application until API, DNS, storage, identity prerequisites and independent administration pass.
- An isolated host-loss exercise restores the selected environment and its data; host/cluster ownership, supported version boundaries and verified recovery results are complete.

### Separate environment acceptance

An isolated empty host and real restore media are required. The current repository does not provision this cluster; the future automation and restore exercise must provide the evidence.

### Dependencies

No dependency on another entry in this register is established.

### Evidence boundary

Source inspection only; no test rerun and no live acceptance performed.

- **recorded verification:** No execution occurred during the recorded source inspection.

## IFR-06-001

**SPIRE persistence, certificate lifetime and recovery contract is incomplete**

Status: open. Severity: medium.

### Problem and impact

The effective CA/server persistence and TTL contract and rotation/restore evidence across certificate expiry are incomplete.

Server, agent or CA loss may interrupt mutual authentication and active jobs. SDS rotation does not establish immediate revocation of already issued SVIDs.

### Components and current state

- SPIRE server/agent
- CSI workload API
- Envoy SDS
- Worker identities

Values and peer bindings are documented. Historical upstream defaults do not establish the effective rendered recommendations or an actual recovery-time guarantee.

### Remaining work

- Fully render the currently pinned charts and determine server PVC/datastore, CA retention, SVID/CA TTL and effective permissions.
- Specify secured CA/server state, credential authority, tolerated outage and revocation limits.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- Test valid and invalid identities against real consumers and observe SVID renewal over multiple intervals.
- Keep server and agent separately unavailable beyond certificate expiry, then restore CA/server state and resume active jobs.

### Completion criteria

- Only valid peers connect; certificate expiry or an unknown CA never enables fail-open behavior.
- Restore and renewed mutual authentication satisfy the documented operational contract.

### Separate environment acceptance

Actual SPIRE/Envoy/worker execution across certificate expiry is required. Rendering alone does not close this finding.

### Dependencies

No dependency on another entry in this register is established.

### Evidence boundary

Source inspection only; no test rerun and no live acceptance performed.

- **recorded verification:** No execution occurred during the recorded source inspection.
- **implementation commit:** Not established.

### Sources

- [my-values/infra/spire-values.yaml](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ad67f9bb5c75cfa8cc1b926668aec1dd0168452c/my-values/infra/spire-values.yaml) — Commit-pinned source or historical evidence; current interpretation and limits are stated above.

## IFR-16-001

**Combined node and disk capacity is not fully budgeted and measured**

Status: open. Severity: medium.

### Problem and impact

Actual node/disk capacity and shared reserves for all applications, jobs, caches, backups and upgrades are not completely budgeted and measured.

Scheduling requests do not prevent shared disk pressure; concurrent builds, restores and browser work may also impair Paperless.

### Components and current state

- Node allocatable
- PVC/ephemeral storage
- Runtime caches
- Prism DB/artifacts/backups
- Paperless

Stateful image/chart pins and preflight checks have partial fixes. Historical storage-review totals are not current measurements. The optional host-pool profile is a configuration budget, not observed available capacity.

### Remaining work

- Combine current rendered requests/limits and actual allocatable/disk values, including DaemonSets, surge, jobs and Paperless reserve.
- Budget ephemeral/PVC/cache/backup growth and align quotas with permitted manual retention.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- Schedule the entire actually selected configuration with maximum planned concurrent job, upgrade and restore load.
- In an isolated environment, exercise a deliberate disk boundary and measure quota handling, Paperless latency and recovery.

### Completion criteria

- The complete resource budget matches actual placement and has measured reserve.
- Disk/quota exhaustion is controlled and the critical application and recovery remain within the agreed operating contract.

### Separate environment acceptance

Real scheduling, load and disk measurements are required. Requests alone do not prove free host resources.

### Dependencies

No dependency on another entry in this register is established.

## IFR-26-001

**Complete independent application recovery is not yet demonstrated**

Status: in-progress. Severity: high.

### Problem and impact

A complete independently recoverable set of database, artifacts, required keys/journals and identities, followed by application recovery, remains incomplete.

After host or volume loss, database references may be unreadable or recovery identities unavailable. A backup on the same failure-domain PVC is insufficient.

### Components and current state

- Prism backup job
- PostgreSQL
- Content-addressed ArtifactStore
- Keys/worker journals
- External backup failure domain

The job now captures a database dump followed by immutable artifacts into a verified group with quotas and no automatic deletion. Seven real file/process/Helm tests use explicit SQL fixtures; they are not native SQL, DB-reference or full DR evidence.

### Remaining work

- Run the original pinned PostgreSQL image and schema with the backup program and verify every restored database artifact reference.
- Bind required external keys, journals and identities into an explicit recovery set with defined ownership.
- Configure an independent external failure domain, access, retention and recovery-time contract; demonstrate a full restore to a fresh target.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- TMPDIR=/dev/shm HELM_BIN=/path/to/helm node --test tests/verification/deployment/prism-backup.test.mts (existing filesystem/process/render coverage; SQL remains a fixture).
- Restore a real backup group to another namespace/host. Read digest objects with original readers, follow DB references and resume application sessions/jobs and the pipeline path.
- Reject missing/corrupt objects, keys and incomplete groups separately. pg_restore --list alone is insufficient.

### Completion criteria

- All required data and external recovery identities are bound and usable on a fresh independent target.
- Real PostgreSQL/artifact references and the complete application path work after restore; declared RPO/RTO are demonstrated.

### Separate environment acceptance

Real SQL/image/cross-store/host recovery remains pending. A weekly same-server SQL smoke check is not host-loss evidence.

### Dependencies

No dependency on another entry in this register is established.

### Evidence boundary

Source inspection only; no test rerun and no live acceptance performed.

## IFR-28-001

**Independent recovery outside the Ops Pod is unproved**

Status: open. Severity: medium.

### Problem and impact

The Ops Pod depends on cluster scheduling, API, PVC, CNI and potentially cluster DNS. Independent host/KVM recovery has not been demonstrated.

When those foundations fail, the Codex devbox may also become unreachable. Pairing or appserver readiness does not establish disaster recovery.

### Components and current state

- Ops Pod/Codex devbox
- Host/KVM/SSH access
- Tailscale
- CNI/API/PVC

Independent host access is an operator statement. Current chart defaults use execNamespaces=[kubeclaw] and mount a token/kubeconfig in Codex; the historical observer-only description is not the current permission contract. MCP tool mode and Kubernetes identity must be distinguished.

### Remaining work

- Document the cluster-dependent convenience path and independent host/KVM/external recovery path with separate credentials, DNS/network prerequisites and responsibilities.
- Capture the actual rendered Codex/MCP permissions. execNamespaces=[] disables optional exec access but does not create independent recovery access.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- In an authorized scenario, separately fail Argo, Tailscale/DNS and CNI; authenticate through independent host access and restore the desired configuration.
- Verify PVC/appserver recovery and actual Codex authentication. Pairing status is not proof of host recovery.

### Completion criteria

- Independent access works when cluster-dependent paths fail, with recovery artifacts and credentials still accessible.
- Actual permission, authentication and recovery boundaries are demonstrated.

### Separate environment acceptance

Independent recovery and real Codex pairing remain pending; this documentation introduces no permission expansion.

### Dependencies

No dependency on another entry in this register is established.

### Evidence boundary

Source inspection only; no test rerun and no live acceptance performed.

- **recorded verification:** No execution occurred during the recorded source inspection.
- **implementation commit:** Not established.

## GITOPS-REVISION-001

**Continuous GitOps health compares a branch name with resolved commit IDs**

Status: open. Severity: unassessed.

### Problem and impact

continuousApplications sets runtime child targetRevision=main, but strict application-health.lua requires status.sync.revision and operationState.syncResult.revision to equal that literal targetRevision. A resolved commit SHA does not equal main.

An actually synchronized healthy runtime child reporting its SHA can remain Progressing in the app-of-apps gate and block later waves. This is a source-confirmed mismatch, not an observed live outage.

### Components and current state

- scripts/gitops-continuous.mjs
- charts/gitops/files/application-health.lua
- Runtime app-of-apps

Source inspection identified the mismatch in integrated main. Existing health tests cover exact commit pins, stale-operation rejection and separate observed platform mode, but contain no positive continuous main-with-resolved-SHA case.

### Remaining work

- Bind the selected and actually synchronized immutable revision consistently while continuous manifests track main.
- Preserve stale-operation, source-path, destination, error and drift checks. Removing revision comparisons or switching runtime children to observed mode is not sufficient.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- Invoke the original Lua with spec.source.targetRevision="main", status.sync.status="Synced", status.sync.revision="aaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa", health.status="Healthy", operationState.phase="Succeeded" and syncResult.revision set to that same SHA. comparedTo.source must match spec.source including main/path/repoURL/directory.include; comparedTo.destination must match spec.destination. Omit observed mode. Current code returns Progressing.
- Use the immutable-SHA positive fixture in tests/verification/deployment/gitops-health.test.mjs and change only spec.source.targetRevision and comparedTo.source.targetRevision to main. Test current and stale operation revisions separately.

### Completion criteria

- The selected real continuous commit can reach Healthy when sync, source binding, successful operation and workload health all match it.
- Stale or mismatched successful operations remain blocked; ComparisonError, drift, changed paths and destination changes retain their protections.
- Runtime and manually synchronized platform health remain separate contracts.

### Separate environment acceptance

After correction, accept an actual branch-to-SHA rollout with the subsequent wave and a stale operation. Lua fixtures alone do not establish live acceptance.

### Dependencies

No dependency on another entry in this register is established.

### Evidence boundary

The inspection covered both original sources and the existing health test. Deterministic mismatch follows from string comparison. No Lua or Argo execution occurred.


### Sources

- [scripts/gitops-continuous.mjs](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ad67f9bb5c75cfa8cc1b926668aec1dd0168452c/scripts/gitops-continuous.mjs) — Commit-pinned source or historical evidence; current interpretation and limits are stated above.

## PRISM-PREFERENCE-001

**Accepted no-decay preference contract conflicts with automatic 180-day decay**

Status: open. Severity: unassessed.

### Problem and impact

The accepted prism-preference-learning-v1 document explicitly excludes automatic time decay, while projectPreferences computes score * 0.5^(ageDays/180) and createPreferenceGeneration persists policyVersion=prism.preferences.v1.decay180-project-override.

Readers cannot determine whether preferences should remain stable with age or weaken automatically. Different contract interpretations can produce different effective preferences for the same event history.

### Components and current state

- Prism preference projection
- Preference generation snapshots
- D11 accepted preference contract

Both current implementation files and the accepted no-decay statements were inspected at the source baseline. Tests explicitly cover decay and snapshot policy identity. No authoritative approval superseding the no-decay rule was identified in this bounded reconciliation; that approval state remains unknown rather than inferred from code.

### Remaining work

- Resolve the contract explicitly: retain the accepted no-decay rule or document an approved replacement specifying the intended temporal policy.
- Align implementation, policyVersion, documentation and regression expectations with that decision. Preserve event provenance, retraction, referenceTime, project-over-personal behavior and deterministic snapshot replay; do not silently reinterpret historical snapshots.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- Inspect docs/architecture/prism-preference-learning-v1.md. V1 excludes automatic time decay in the opening scope and time-handling section. Compare skills/prism/preferences/index.ts projectPreferences and skills/prism/control/preference-snapshot.ts.
- Use one valid selected event with a single trait and evaluate the original projector at its last evidence time and 180 days later. Current arithmetic yields score1/effectiveScore1, then score1/effectiveScore0.5. Preserve user and project context with all required event fields. The source inspection did not execute the probe.
- Existing regression entry points: skills/prism/tests/quality.test.mts (preference projections decay and remain retractable) and skills/prism/tests/control-generation-http.test.mts (persisted decay policy identity).

### Completion criteria

- One explicit accepted policy resolves the contradiction without treating implemented behavior as implicit approval.
- Projection tests, persisted policy identity and published contract agree, including fixed-reference-time replay and event retraction.
- Any historical snapshot compatibility or migration rule is explicit; approval and implementation states remain distinguishable.

### Separate environment acceptance

This is a contract/implementation alignment task that can be verified locally. It does not assert a deployed incident or reopen an original 154 finding.

### Dependencies

No dependency on another entry in this register is established.

### Evidence boundary

Bounded source and existing-test inspection; no preference test execution, product change or inferred policy approval.


### Sources

- [skills/prism/preferences/index.ts](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/ad67f9bb5c75cfa8cc1b926668aec1dd0168452c/skills/prism/preferences/index.ts) — Accepted contract, current implementation or existing regression; conflict described above.

## PRISM-DEPLOY-CHECK-001

**Prism deployment source check is stale after prompt ownership moved**

Status: open. Severity: medium.

### Problem and impact

The Prism deployment source check requires the canonical contract paths as literal text in both the values file and agent-bridge.mjs. The bridge now delegates prompt construction to agent-prompt.mjs, which owns those paths.

npm run verify:prism:deploy-script fails before installation even though the active prompt owner contains the required paths. The documented installation preflight therefore stops until the check follows the current ownership boundary.

### Components and current state

- Prism deployment verification
- Prism agent bridge
- Prism agent prompt
- Prism installation preflight

A documentation verification run reproduced the failure on 2026-09-16. The assertion reads agent-bridge.mjs directly and does not follow its AgentJobRunner and prompt-module boundary. The documentation reports the failed check and does not claim Prism preflight success.

### Remaining work

- Update the source check to inspect the active prompt owner and its wiring from the bridge without duplicating production prompt text in the test.
- Keep the negative check that rejects project-checkout contract paths and preserve all unrelated deployment assertions.
- Run the complete verify:prism:deploy-script command and refresh the evidence status only after it passes.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- Run npm run verify:prism:deploy-script at the recorded source. Observe the canonical-schema assertion failure.
- Compare tests/verification/contracts/check-deploy-prism-command.mts with skills/prism/server/agent-bridge.mjs and skills/prism/server/agent-prompt.mjs.

### Completion criteria

- The source check follows the real prompt ownership boundary and verifies both canonical bundle paths.
- npm run verify:prism:deploy-script exits with status zero without weakening its deployment, image, Secret, migration, or negative-path assertions.
- The installation guide records the successful rerun and retains the distinction between source verification and live deployment.

### Separate environment acceptance

This check can close through source verification. It does not establish a successful Prism deployment or replace the separate live acceptance gates.

### Dependencies

No dependency on another entry in this register is established.

### Evidence boundary

Reproduced during documentation verification; no product or test implementation changed.

- **recorded verification:** npm run verify:prism:deploy-script exited with status 1 on 2026-09-16 at the canonical-schema assertion.

### Sources

- [tests/verification/contracts/check-deploy-prism-command.mts](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/85e73b1885f04a9494f388cf6622ad0bde2db447/tests/verification/contracts/check-deploy-prism-command.mts) — The failing literal-path assertion and the surrounding deployment checks.
- [skills/prism/server/agent-bridge.mjs](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/85e73b1885f04a9494f388cf6622ad0bde2db447/skills/prism/server/agent-bridge.mjs) — The current bridge delegates durable agent work and does not own prompt text.

## PLUGIN-BOUNDARY-001

Status: open. Severity: medium.

### Problem and impact

The Buster quality-gate stage imports assertion functions from the root of @kubeclaw/pipeline-test-gate-contract. The plugin boundary check deliberately permits only audited exact exports for stage dependency graphs and includes a negative test that rejects this package-root import.

The complete plugin boundary verification stops before it can certify the current extension boundary. Documentation can describe the intended exact-export rule, but it cannot claim that every installed stage currently complies with that rule.

### Components and current state

- Buster quality-gate stage
- Pipeline test-gate contract
- Plugin-system v2 boundary verification
- Extension documentation

A focused verification run reproduced the failure on 2026-09-16 after generating the required OpenClaw contract output. The platform-configuration, contract, registry and runtime-role checks pass. The boundary check then fails at skills/nova/plugins/buster-quality-gate/src/stage.ts line 1. The same stage already uses the approved gate-decision subpath for other functions.

### Remaining work

- Expose the required coverage assertion API through an audited exact contract export. If needed, define another narrow boundary that preserves the test's authority controls.
- Change the quality-gate stage to use the accepted narrow entry point. Do not weaken the negative package-root test merely to make the check pass.
- Run the complete plugin-system v2 boundary check and update the evidence only after it exits with status zero.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- Run npm run build --workspace @kubeclaw/openclaw-agent-observer so that the boundary check can inspect its generated contract module.
- Run node tests/verification/contracts/check-plugin-system-v2-boundaries.mjs. Observe: stage cannot import an unapproved runtime package: skills/nova/plugins/buster-quality-gate/src/stage.ts:1 -> @kubeclaw/pipeline-test-gate-contract.
- Compare the root import in skills/nova/plugins/buster-quality-gate/src/stage.ts with the exact-export allowlist and package-root negative assertions in tests/verification/contracts/check-plugin-system-v2-boundaries.mjs.

### Completion criteria

- The quality-gate stage imports its runtime contract only through explicitly audited exact exports.
- The package-root negative tests remain effective and the complete plugin-system v2 boundary check exits with status zero.
- Extension documentation links to the resulting supported boundary and does not turn an implementation exception into a documented feature.

### Separate environment acceptance

This source-boundary issue can close with local source and contract verification. It does not establish runtime activation or a live pipeline execution.

### Dependencies

No dependency on another entry in this register is established.

### Evidence boundary

A focused source inspection reproduced the issue. It compared documentation, source, and verification without changing product or test implementation.

- **recorded verification:** The boundary command exited with status 1 on 2026-09-16 after the required generated OpenClaw contract became available.

## EFFECT-RECONCILIATION-001

**Uncertain external effects have no supported reconciliation and result-import operation**

Status: open. Severity: high.

### Problem and impact

Effect recovery correctly stops when an external service accepts a request without returning a trustworthy receipt. It also stops when a receipt exists without terminal attempt evidence. The current platform supplies no supported operation that records reconciliation and imports the authoritative result.

An operator can identify an uncertain effect but cannot continue the run through a documented, validated state transition. Blind retry can duplicate an external mutation, while journal editing would bypass lifecycle authority.

### Components and current state

- Nova effect recovery
- Administrative retry and remediation
- External capability adapters
- Effectful extension path

Source tracing followed the recovery guard through normal execution and administrative retry. Both paths stop on unresolved external outcomes. The effectful guide states this limit and does not invent a continuation command.

### Remaining work

- Define a versioned reconciliation request and result contract with actor identity, effect identity, evidence, idempotency and authorization.
- Implement one Core-owned operation that records the decision and imports or compensates the result without editing journals.
- Add failure, duplicate, cancellation, restart and audit tests, then document the supported operator and extension behavior.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- Run the persistent external-effect recovery tests in the verification record.
- Create an accepted external effect without a receipt, then attempt normal resume and administrative retry. Observe that both paths return the unresolved-outcome guard.
- Inspect skills/nova/core/execution/effect-recovery.ts, engine-run.ts and engine-admin.ts. Confirm that no supported reconciliation import operation follows the stop.

### Completion criteria

- An authorized operator can reconcile one uncertain effect through a supported API without direct journal changes.
- The operation rejects mismatched effect, attempt, actor and evidence identities and remains idempotent after restart.
- The effectful extension guide includes the exact operation, observations, failure paths and retained evidence.

### Separate environment acceptance

Local contract and restart tests can prove the state transition. A real external service remains a separate live acceptance exercise.

### Dependencies

No dependency on another entry in this register is established.

### Evidence boundary

Independent source trace and local recovery exercises; no reconciliation implementation was added.

- **recorded verification:** The review confirmed that normal, retry and remediation paths preserve the recovery stop.

### Sources

- [skills/nova/core/execution/effect-recovery.ts](https://github.com/datrab/kubeclaw/blob/bcf032f241b432bf920baa9ee5f727947921447d/skills/nova/core/execution/effect-recovery.ts) — The recovery guard rejects unresolved and externally incomplete effects.

## RUNTIME-VERIFICATION-001

**Four runtime verification paths fail before they prove their contracts**

Status: open. Severity: medium.

### Problem and impact

A supported-host run observed failures in the test-plan runner, report-adapter runtime, runtime-bundle isolation and transport-publisher checks. The failures are distinct, but their product or host root causes are not yet established.

The extension guide can document intended contracts and exact observed limits. It cannot use these commands as successful local evidence before diagnosis and a successful rerun.

### Components and current state

- Buster test-plan runner
- Buster report-adapter runtime
- Runtime bundle isolation
- Transport publisher

The verification record contains exact command output. The plan runner returned errored instead of timed_out. The report adapter ended with EPIPE. Isolation could not open task children. Transport publication rejected the canonical effect request. Later environments can expose different prerequisite failures; those do not erase the supported-host observations.

### Remaining work

## PRISM-TOOL-LIMITS-001

**Prism OpenClaw tools lack general payload and request-lifetime limits**

Status: open. Severity: medium.

### Problem and impact

The Prism OpenClaw extension bounds the number of designs but does not define general text or document size limits. Its HTTP request also has no explicit timeout or cancellation signal.

A large request or stalled Prism control connection can retain host resources for an undefined period. Extension authors cannot copy a complete bounded-call pattern from this package.

### Components and current state

- Prism OpenClaw extension
- Prism control client
- Host extension guidance

The guide no longer describes the existing Prism tools as fully bounded. It distinguishes requirements for a new extension from behavior that Prism currently implements.

### Remaining work

- Approve explicit request-size, text-size and document-size limits for both Prism tools.
- Add an explicit timeout and cancellation propagation contract to the HTTP call.
- Test boundary values, cancellation, timeout, host registration and error mapping, then update the package page.

### Reproduction and verification procedure

- Inspect skills/prism/openclaw-plugin/index.mjs and identify the design-count constraint.
- Confirm that the parameter schemas do not set complete text/document bounds and that the fetch call has no timeout or cancellation signal.
- Run the current registration tests and observe that they check names and design count, not a real host request lifetime.

### Completion criteria

- Approved schemas bound all request-controlled payloads or record a justified alternative resource boundary.
- The client enforces a documented timeout and propagates cancellation without committing a partial revision.
- Tests exercise limits and real host registration, and the host-extension guide states the verified behavior.

### Separate environment acceptance

Local schema and cancellation tests are required first. A real OpenClaw-to-Prism call remains separate live evidence.

### Dependencies

No dependency on another entry in this register is established.

### Evidence boundary

Independent source and registration-test inspection; no product implementation changed.

- **recorded verification:** The package registration test passed but did not establish a bounded real-host request.
